task1.title: Percentage of Australian men and women doing regular physical activity, 2010
task1.prompt: The bar chart below shows the percentage of Australian men and women in different age groups who did regular physical activity in 2010.

chartDesc.title: Percentage of Australian men and women doing regular physical activity: 2010
chartDesc.overview: Overall, females generally had higher rates of regular physical activity than males in most age categories, except in the youngest group (15 to 24) where males were more active. Physical activity among men reached its lowest point in the middle age groups before rising again, whereas female participation remained consistently high from ages 25 to 64.
keyFeatures: Highest percentage for females was in the 45 to 54 age group at 53.3%.
Lowest overall percentage was recorded for males aged 35 to 44 at 39.5%.
Males were higher than females only in the 15 to 24 age group (52.8% for males vs 47.7% for females).
The 65 and over age category had almost equal participation rates between men (46.7%) and women (47.1%).

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

task2.title: Sharing information in research and business
task2.prompt:
Some people believe that it is good to share as much information as possible in scientific research, business and the academic world. Others believe that some information is too important or too valuable to be shared freely.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
